mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < 500k) signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer confidence and corporate earnings pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic output, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in CPI inflation below 2% combined with a federal funds rate below 1% signals a low-rate, low-inflation environment that supports risk asset valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 102 AND FEDFUNDS < 1% in the same month
regime_hint: low inflation and low rates regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the previous six-month average, alongside a concurrent decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (implied from GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving that typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 6-month average AND GDPC1 growth YoY < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which typically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -1% AND HOUST < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.
